divya: Thinking ahead — we should discuss a long-term refactor for residency enforcement. Current ad-hoc flags are getting messy when we chain fallbacks. Idea: a declarative residency contract that lives in the control plane and gets compiled into routing policies.

mike: +1. can you sketch what the contract looks like?

divya: Rough sketch: each tenant has a small contract blob like `regionPolicy: [eu_only | prefer_eu | global]`, `fallback: [deny | allow_with_audit | allow]`, `dataClass: [pii | general]`. The compiler emits router rules, preflight checks, and an operator-visible diff for cutovers.

sara: sounds neat. how would we handle short-lived fallbacks for outages? e.g., prefer_eu but allow_us_when_eu_down for 15m.

divya: we can add a `fallbackWindow` and `telemetrySLA` fields. The runtime enforces emergency valve with strict TTL and auto-revoke. operator can also set `consentEscalation: manual | automatic` to control legal gating.

jonathan: couple of tradeoffs: 1) routing complexity -> more RTTs if we probe region eligibility. 2) config explosion if each tenant has rich blobs. 3) migration complexity.

leah: for migration complexity, we should design a 3-step rollout: preview (dry-run), shadow (route but don't charge), commit. That mirrors what we do for model rollouts.

mike: implementation thoughts: plumb contracts into the existing proxy as a small policy engine. We already have `region-hint` headers; compiler would emit a compact policy token the proxy can interpret w/o extra RPCs. e.g., `X-RW-Residency: token-v1:abcd`

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment started for `residency-compiler` on staging-2 at 14:08 UTC :rocket:

sara: metrics we need: failover-rate per-tenant, cross-region egress cost delta, avg added latency for preferring remote. also a count of times `allow_with_audit` is used.

divya: agree. also we should log decision provenance: which contract version, which compiled policy id, and operator override id if present.

jonathan: one more: KV cache ownership. If we redirect writes during fallback the cache semantics break. we need an escrow pattern or sticky write-leases. otherwise cold cache thrash will blow tail latency.

leah: proposal: add `kvOwnership` hint in contract: `owner_region` + `stale_ttl` + `reconcile_mode`. Runtime either proxies writes (forward) or accepts and marks for async reconciliation based on `reconcile_mode`.

mike: reconcile_mode options: `sync_forward`, `async_sweep`, `eventual_merge`. each has different latency and cost tradeoffs. default to `async_sweep` with operator opt-in for `sync_forward`.

divya: rollout plan: 1) spec PR + contract schema, 2) residency compiler MVP that outputs policy tokens, 3) proxy change to understand tokens + dry-run mode, 4) operator console UI for previews, 5) canary with small tenants.

sara: who owns the spec PR?

divya: i'll draft the PR and add design doc pointers. mike and jonathan can review the compile/runtime bits. leah will own operator runbook and console UX.

mike: edge cases: what if two tenants share data boundaries (multi-tenant DB shard)? contract must include `sharedResource` flags so router can block partial fallbacks.

jonathan: and we must think about billing: if fallback causes cross-region egress we need explicit opt-in per tenant or a hard deny for EU-only customers. billing should be surfaced on preview.

leah: runbook note: include an emergency `revoke` button that marks a contract as temporarily disabled and forces local routing. ops-bot should emit an audit event and require two-person approval for EU-restricted accounts.

divya: question for the group: do we want the compiler to treat contracts as first-class objects in our config DB (versioned, auditable) or ephemeral overlays? I prefer versioned objects.

sara: versioned objects + immutable history. lets us roll back and reason about incidents.

mike: small POC suggestion: implement compiler as a lambda that takes contract JSON -> policy token + human diff. start with 3 fields: `regionPolicy`, `fallback`, `kvOwnership`. keep rest optional.

jonathan: test plan: simulate cross-region outage in chaos env, measure cold cache penalty under each `reconcile_mode`, and validate that `allow_with_audit` produces an audit trail but no silent egress.

leah: thumbs up. I’ll draft runbook sections: preflight checks, revoke, required approvals, and cost dashboard alerts.

divya: thanks everyone. I'll post the PR link when it's ready. tagging @mike @leah @jonathan for reviews. :memo:

mike: looking forward to it. small nit: ensure the token format can be expanded without breaking proxies. use `v1:` prefix.

ops-bot: ci-bot: residency-spec PR #142 opened by divya — tests pending.

sara: perfect. keep the initial schema tight so we can iterate.

divya: agreed. i’ll include a basic JSON Schema + examples in the PR.

jonathan: sounds good. we should also plan a doc for security review (KMS impact when data routes change).

leah: added to my todo.

mike: ok closing out from my side. low-risk incremental plan is the right path.

divya: closing thread — will link PR. thanks all. :sparkles:
